content:
Wu Chi-wai travelled to the UK last week to visit family members and was initially refused entry before being allowed in. According to the Associated Press, he was only granted seven days' entry, and his air ticket was changed to require his return to Hong Kong this Wednesday (29th). Wu had originally planned to stay in the UK for several months. He denied seeking asylum in Britain, but said his long-term plan was to reunite with his family there. He is also concerned about Hong Kong people facing similar border issues.

In an interview with the Associated Press, Wu Chi-wai said he was visiting his family in the UK. He was worried his criminal record might affect his entry and had communicated with the British consulate beforehand. However, when he arrived at a London airport last Wednesday, border officials believed he might have other intentions, including seeking long-term residence. Wu said he was ultimately granted entry, with authorities permitting him to enter on "bail" for seven days, requiring him to leave the UK this Wednesday (29th). He had originally planned to spend several months with his family this time. He also expressed concern that the entry record would affect his future travels, and hoped the British Home Office would extend his stay.

He said: "I am very worried about whether I have the ability or opportunity to be granted entry to the UK again to reunite with my family." The British Home Office said it generally does not comment on individual cases, and that the government firmly supports Hong Kong people in the UK.

The Associated Press cited Wu Chi-wai as denying that he was seeking asylum in Britain, but said his long-term plan was to reunite with his family there. He is also concerned about Hong Kong people facing similar border issues. He said he had a return ticket, originally scheduled for November, which had been changed to Wednesday, but the change was not made by him. The British Home Office and the airline did not respond to the Associated Press's enquiries.

Former Democratic Party chairman Wu Chi-wai travelled from Hong Kong to the UK on the evening of the 21st of this month and was detained at Heathrow Airport. The Times reported last week that he would be deported back within seven days. Wu was sentenced to 4 years and 5 months' imprisonment in the 47 defendants case and was released on 30 June upon completing his sentence.
